newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul banks agree on 80.4 bln won Jinro bail-out.
newsitem.headline: Seoul banks agree on 80.4 bln won Jinro bail-out.

text.p: A committee of South Korean commercial banks on Monday agreed to extend 80.4 billion won in emergency loans to bail out six affiliates of the troubled Jinro Group.
The emergency loans would be made "as soon as possible", a committee official said.

The official of the Commercial Bank of Korea said the loans would be supplied after Jinro Group chairman Chang Jin-ho issues a letter allowing banks to dispose of his family's shareholding in group affiliates.
It was unclear whether Chang had already agreed to give up his family's ownership and management rights in the group.
An earlier decision to defer debt payments for the six core affiliates of the group will be in effect until July 21, the official told reporters after the committee meeting.
The 19th-ranked Jinro Group buckled under 3.2 trillion won in debt, mostly a result of reckless expansion.
The group has said it would sell part of its property and affiliates to raise an estimated 1.2 trillion won by the end of 1998 for debt repayment.
The group's flagship and the nation's largest distilled liquor maker, Jinro Ltd, will get 25.1 billion won of the planned emergency loans, the official said.
Earlier on Monday South Korea's 30 merchant banks said they had agreed to join the committee after commercial banks accepted their demand to exempt them from offering additional credit.
